nodes.label: BD-Citizenlink Citizen Registry Prototype
nodes.rationale: Built to test whether a graph database can replace relational storage for a national civil registry, giving sub-second multi-generational relationship queries that repeated self-joins on a 170M-row table cannot.

nodes.label: _compute_all_relationships BFS Labeling
nodes.rationale: Builds an adjacency list annotated with UP/DOWN/SPOUSE direction so every node on the canvas carries a named label rather than a raw hop count.

nodes.label: /api/birth-audit Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Targets the real fraud of registering a child twice to shift their recorded age; consecutive births are sorted by DOB and judged on the day gap.

nodes.label: categorizeSide Two-Hop Side Categorization
nodes.rationale: Cousins need a grandparent check one hop beyond the connecting uncle, otherwise a maternal cousin is wrongly routed to the father's side through the root.

nodes.label: D3.js Force-Directed Family Tree Canvas
nodes.rationale: Force parameters are tuned by tree size (charge, collision radius, alphaDecay) so small trees settle faster while large ones spread far enough to stay legible.

nodes.label: /api/family-tree Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Runs a fixed sequence of queries regardless of family size, which is why latency stays at 44-90 ms whether the tree holds 20 or 97 people.

nodes.label: Half-Sibling Detection via Shared-Parent Map
nodes.rationale: An UP,DOWN move pair is only a half-sibling when exactly one parent is shared, so the classifier consults the parents map rather than trusting the path shape.

nodes.label: inject_multiple_marriages.py Polygamy Injection Utility
nodes.rationale: A fresh regeneration of the 1 GB CSV changes every NID and invalidates saved demo cases, so polygynous households are grafted onto the existing dataset and emitted as a small polygamy_delta.csv instead.

nodes.label: Neo4j Graph Schema (:Citizen, HAS_FATHER, HAS_MOTHER, MARRIED_TO)
nodes.norm_label: neo4j graph schema (:citizen, has_father, has_mother, married_to)
nodes.rationale: One node label and three relationship types keep traversal cheap; MARRIED_TO is undirected so a polygynous man simply carries up to four of the same edge type instead of needing a separate schema.

nodes.label: neo4j_import.py Two-Pass Importer
nodes.rationale: Two passes are used because relationship creation must MATCH nodes that already exist; it also takes an optional CSV argument so a small delta file can be imported without reloading the 1 GB dataset.

nodes.label: 13-Digit NID Format (Rule 31)
nodes.rationale: 4-digit birth year plus 2-digit district code plus 7 random digits, echoing how real NIDs encode birth information and geography, though the exact digit layout is simplified.

nodes.label: Polygyny Wife-Count Selection Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Only married Muslim men roll for extra wives (2 wives 8%, 3 wives 3%, 4 wives 1%), mirroring Islamic law and Bangladeshi legality; rates are set slightly generous compared with real prevalence so the feature is visible in demos.

nodes.label: Relational NID Storage Problem
nodes.rationale: Tables answer single-person lookups well but need repeated self-joins to walk a lineage; over 170 million citizens that cost becomes administrative delay and an opening for identity fraud.

nodes.label: Move-Sequence Relationship Classification
nodes.rationale: Order-sensitive rules run before count-based rules because three different relationships sit at exactly 2 hops (co-wife, step-mother, half-sibling); a pure hop-counting classifier cannot tell them apart, so the order of SPOUSE/UP/DOWN moves is read instead.

nodes.label: _relationship_detail Explanation Line
nodes.rationale: Supplies the auditable justification the thesis argues black-box AI cannot give: 'same father' or 'shares husband Karim Ahmed' names the evidence behind the label.

nodes.label: /api/relationship Shortest-Path Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Uses Neo4j's built-in shortestPath over HAS_FATHER|HAS_MOTHER|MARRIED_TO with a 20-hop cap; beyond roughly 19 hops the answer degrades to a generic description rather than a real kinship name, so raising the cap buys little.

nodes.label: Research Gap: Speed vs Legal Transparency vs Live Updates
nodes.norm_label: research gap: speed vs legal transparency vs live updates
nodes.rationale: Static-index graph systems must re-index the whole national database on every birth, while AI matchers are black boxes a government cannot lawfully cite when refusing a visa; no existing system combines graph speed with auditable reasoning and real-time updates.

nodes.label: /api/search Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Branches on whether the query is all digits: NID prefix goes through STARTS WITH on the index, anything else falls back to a case-insensitive CONTAINS scan.

nodes.label: Synthetic Bangladeshi Citizen Dataset (5,130,495 records)
nodes.rationale: Real NID data is legally confidential and unobtainable, so the project generates its own four-generation population under rules copied from real Bangladeshi demographics; this also gives other researchers a testable dataset without breaking privacy law.

nodes.label: 47 System Rules
nodes.rationale: Rules 1-33 govern generation, 34-45 govern relationship reading and input validation, and 46-47 were added with the multiple-marriage upgrade.

nodes.label: Public Administration Use Cases
nodes.rationale: Birth registration auditing, visa and passport verification, social welfare distribution, inheritance verification, and criminal alias detection all reduce to structural questions about the family graph.

nodes.label: validate_data.py Consistency Checker
nodes.rationale: Realistic rules mean nothing if the generator silently breaks them, so 13 read-only Cypher checks measure the imported graph against the rule groups rather than asserting compliance in prose.

nodes.label: Edge and Ring Visual Encoding
nodes.rationale: Every colour, ring and line style carries a fixed meaning so half-siblings, step-relations and multiple marriages are readable at a glance; marriage links curve so a man's several wives fan out instead of overlapping.

nodes.label: Answer Size Dominates Database Size
nodes.rationale: Every query starts at an indexed NID and walks only the local neighbourhood, so growing 5M to 50M records would barely move the 13-90 ms bars; the length of the walk depends on the family, not the population. This is the central claim a relational join plan cannot match.

nodes.label: Batched MERGE Import (10,000-row UNWIND)
nodes.rationale: One row per transaction would take forever at 5M records, and MERGE rather than CREATE makes the import idempotent so a re-run cannot duplicate nodes or edges.

nodes.label: Zero Flagged Pairs: Year-Granular Birth Dates
nodes.norm_label: zero flagged pairs: year-granular birth dates
nodes.rationale: Across 2,000 couples and 6,741 pairs the audit flagged nothing, not because detection works but because the generator spaces siblings by whole years and fixes every child's birthday at 15 June, so gaps are either 0 or at least 365 days and the 1-269 day window can never be reached. The same cause inflates the twin rate to 11.3%. Day-level birthdays are the fix.

nodes.label: Neo4j Cold-Start Warm-Up
nodes.rationale: The first query after a restart takes seconds while page cache and query plans build; it is excluded from all reported medians and is worked around by running one query before a demo.

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Realism Justification
nodes.rationale: Two-part argument: the rules mirror real Bangladesh (legal marriage ages 21/18, 2022 census religion mix, division population shares, falling fertility, 17-digit BRNs, patrilineal naming), and validate_data.py measures that the generated data obeys them. Admitted simplifications - six old divisions, fixed birthdays, no death or divorce - are argued not to touch what the project studies.

nodes.label: 300 ms Debounced Search Input
nodes.rationale: Waiting 300 ms after the last keystroke stops every letter from firing its own request, which matters most because an unmatched name costs a full scan.

nodes.label: Edge-Count Integrity Cross-Check
nodes.rationale: HAS_FATHER and HAS_MOTHER both equal 4,347,936 exactly, so no half-built child exists; and 782,559 parentless people decompose exactly into 782,500 generated founders plus 59 injected wives, proving no founder was lost or duplicated in import.

nodes.label: Edge De-duplication
nodes.rationale: Generic parent links are dropped once a typed father/mother version exists, and reciprocal duplicates are collapsed, otherwise D3 would draw double lines.

nodes.label: Graph vs Table Split (GRAPH_HIDE)
nodes.rationale: The API computes every relative but a role-based regex keeps uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews and nieces off the canvas so the drawing stays readable; measured cost is that 62% of a Gen-3 family (23 of 37 people) is only visible in the table.

nodes.label: localhost IPv6 Failover Stall
nodes.rationale: On Windows 'localhost' resolves to ::1 first while the Flask dev server listens on IPv4 only, so every request waits ~2 s for the IPv6 attempt to fail; the app felt slow despite a ~20 ms warm family-tree API. Opening 127.0.0.1:5000 removes the delay entirely.

nodes.label: 270-Day Minimum Birth Gap Threshold
nodes.rationale: 270 days is roughly a full-term pregnancy, so any gap between 1 and 269 days is biologically impossible for one mother; a zero-day gap is exempted because twins and triplets are legitimate.

nodes.label: CONTAINS Name Search Full Scan
nodes.rationale: No index serves CONTAINS, so a query matching nothing must read all 5.13M names: 2,894 ms versus 13 ms for an indexed NID lookup, 222x slower, and users hit it by making a typo. A common name looks fast (25.6 ms) only because LIMIT 20 lets it stop early. Fix is a Neo4j full-text index on full_name.

nodes.label: Citizen.nid Unique Constraint and B-Tree Index
nodes.norm_label: citizen.nid unique constraint and b-tree index
nodes.rationale: The uniqueness constraint is declared partly for the free B-Tree index it creates, keeping NID lookups at O(log n) across 5.13M records; every fast endpoint starts from this index.

nodes.label: _fetch_parents Parent Back-Fill
nodes.rationale: Without back-filling missing parent edges between people already on the canvas, all children of a polygynous man would hang off the father alone instead of splitting into one branch per wife.

nodes.label: Pipe-Separated spouse_nid Column
nodes.rationale: Multiple wives are packed into the single existing spouse_nid CSV column rather than adding columns, because NIDs are pure digits so the '|' separator can never collide with a value; the wife's own column still holds just the husband.

nodes.label: No Authentication or Access Control
nodes.rationale: Any valid NID exposes a full family tree and demographic profile; acceptable in a prototype but a serious breach for a national deployment, so authentication and role-based access are listed as required future work.

nodes.label: Restricted Marriage Expansion (In-Law Exclusion)
nodes.rationale: Marriages are expanded only for the root's own spouses and direct parents, which pulls in co-wives and step-mothers while guaranteeing no in-law is ever fetched; enforced at gather time rather than by hiding labels. The accepted price is that marriage-based visa verification is out of reach for the tree view.

nodes.label: Sibling Gap Rule Holds Only as a Tendency
nodes.norm_label: sibling gap rule holds only as a tendency
nodes.rationale: Child i gets birth year start + i x random(1..4) with an independent roll per child, so siblings can share a year or exceed 4 years apart; only 77.8% of sampled gaps fall in the 1-4 year band. Accumulating each gap onto a running year instead of multiplying by the index would make Rule 3 strict.

nodes.label: nid < sp_nid Marriage Edge Ordering Guard
nodes.norm_label: nid < sp_nid marriage edge ordering guard
nodes.rationale: Marriage is stored on both spouses' rows, so an ordering predicate keeps each undirected MARRIED_TO edge from being created twice, even when one row lists several spouses.

nodes.label: D3.js v7 Force-Directed Family Tree Canvas
nodes.norm_label: d3.js v7 force-directed family tree canvas

nodes.label: D3 Force Simulation and BIG_TREE Tuning
nodes.norm_label: d3 force simulation and big_tree tuning
nodes.rationale: Trees over 150 nodes switch to cheaper settings (charge -300, distanceMax 420, collision 26, alphaDecay 0.05) so a 300+ node founder tree settles instead of stalling the page.

nodes.label: Simulation Stop-Before-Rerender Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Every re-render calls simulation.stop() on the previous simulation; otherwise old simulations pile up on removed nodes, choke the main thread and freeze zoom and pan.

nodes.label: Parentage vs Marriage Edge Encoding
nodes.rationale: Directed arrowheaded lines carry parentage and are gender-coloured (blue father-to-child, pink mother-to-child) so lineage direction and parent sex are readable without labels. Marriage is an undirected amber dash-dot line, and cousin/extended ties are a faint grey dotted line so inferred kinship visually recedes behind recorded facts.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure Landing-to-App Flow
nodes.rationale: One HTML document holds both a marketing-style hero landing view and the working explorer; the app section stays hidden until a citizen is selected, and a back button returns to the hero. This avoids a second page load and lets the D3 canvas and its cached graph state survive navigation between the two views.

nodes.label: Ring-Flag Kinship Visual Encoding
nodes.rationale: Node fill colour is reserved for identity (selected person, male, female, spouse), so kinship qualifiers get an orthogonal channel: coloured node rings. Solid green = full sibling, dashed cyan = half sibling, dashed orange = step relation, dashed rose = co-wife/co-husband, plus a marriage glyph for people with multiple marriages. Dashed versus solid separates full blood ties from partial or affinal ones, so polygamous households read at a glance without adding extra nodes or edges.

nodes.label: Search Progress and Timing Feedback
nodes.rationale: A progress bar reading 'Searching across 50,00,000 records...' plus a post-search elapsed-time readout make the sub-second Neo4j lookup legible as a search over the full 5-million-record corpus, backing the advertised sub-0.5s average query time stat.

nodes.label: Dataset Scale and Integrity Cross-Checks
nodes.rationale: 5,130,495 nodes and 10,161,934 relationships. Identical HAS_FATHER and HAS_MOTHER counts (4,347,936 each) prove no half-built record, and 782,559 parentless people match 782,500 founders plus 59 injected wives, proving no founder was lost in import.

nodes.label: Measured Query Response Times
nodes.rationale: Median warm runs: 13.0ms NID search, 13.8ms profile, 22.6-37.6ms relationship by hop count, 44-90ms family tree, 2,894ms worst-case name search.

nodes.label: Family Tree Construction Results by Generation
nodes.norm_label: family tree construction results by generation
nodes.rationale: All generations land between 44.0 and 48.3ms because the endpoint runs a fixed query set. Gen-3 is the worst case for the canvas: only 14 of 37 people are shown, since a Gen-3 person is the only one with full ancestry above and descendants below.

nodes.label: Government Use Cases
nodes.rationale: Birth registration auditing, immigration and visa verification, social welfare distribution, inheritance verification and criminal investigation via structural overlaps that expose aliases.

nodes.label: BD-Citizenlink Citizen Registry Prototype
nodes.rationale: Prototype built to show that a graph database can model and query complex Bangladeshi family relationships across millions of records with sub-second response times.

nodes.label: generate_nid NID Generation Algorithm
nodes.rationale: 13-digit NID = 4-digit birth year + 2-digit district code + 7 random digits, retried against a used-NID set so no two citizens collide (Rules 29, 31).

nodes.label: inject_multiple_marriages.py Polygamy Injection Utility
nodes.rationale: The full CSV is over 1 GB and a fresh regeneration changes every NID, so polygamous households are injected into the existing dataset and exported as a small polygamy_delta.csv for delta import instead of regenerating.

nodes.label: MARRIED_TO Relationship
nodes.rationale: Undirected marriage link; a polygynous man can carry up to four of these edges.

nodes.label: nid Uniqueness Constraint and B-Tree Index
nodes.norm_label: nid uniqueness constraint and b-tree index
nodes.rationale: The uniqueness constraint on Citizen.nid also creates a B-Tree index for free, giving O(log n) lookups even at 5 million records.

nodes.label: /api/search Endpoint
nodes.rationale: All-digit queries take the STARTS WITH fast path on the B-Tree index; anything else falls back to a CONTAINS scan. Most searches are NID searches, so most hit the fast path.

nodes.label: validate_data.py Consistency Checker
nodes.rationale: Realistic rules mean little if the generator silently breaks them, so the second half of the realism argument is measured (13 read-only Cypher checks) rather than merely asserted.

nodes.label: Validation Results (13 Cypher Checks)
nodes.rationale: Eleven of thirteen checks pass cleanly on 5,130,495 citizens; the two Notes are four out-of-window birth years and the sibling-gap tendency.

nodes.label: Amirhosseini et al. (2024) Graph-Topology Entity Resolution
nodes.norm_label: amirhosseini et al. (2024) graph-topology entity resolution

nodes.label: Citizenlink Graph-Based Registry Framework
nodes.rationale: Proposed because conventional record-oriented databases handle individual records well but cannot efficiently traverse multi-generational relationships, which blocks inheritance, lineage-verification, criminal-analysis and visa use cases.

nodes.label: Lupu et al. (2024) Concurrent Neo4j Path Queries
nodes.norm_label: lupu et al. (2024) concurrent neo4j path queries

nodes.label: Answer Size Matters More Than Database Size
nodes.norm_label: answer size matters more than database size
nodes.rationale: Every query starts at an indexed NID and walks only the nearby graph, never the whole population, so growing from 5M to 50M records would barely move the numbers - the thing a relational design cannot match.

nodes.label: Birth Audit Zero-Flag Null Result
nodes.rationale: Zero flags across 6,741 pairs is not a good result: siblings are spaced by whole years and every child shares a 15 June birthday, so gaps are either 0 or at least 365 days and can never land in the 1-269 day detection window. The audit logic is sound; the dataset simply cannot trigger it.

nodes.label: Population Becomes One Connected Web
nodes.rationale: Two randomly picked unrelated founders were still linked at 19 hops (7 up, 5 marriages, 7 down) because marriages join separate family lines, so after four generations everyone is connected. This validates the 20-hop cap and shows far pairs fall back to a generic description.

nodes.label: Entity Resolution and Deduplication
nodes.rationale: String-similarity record linkage breaks on multi-part ethnonyms, name-order inversion and heterophonic transliteration; topology (shared neighbors, parent-child matches) distinguishes people better than attributes, but deep models leave no auditable trail and MCMC linkage does not scale nationally.

nodes.label: Index-Free Adjacency
nodes.rationale: Each node stores on-disk pointers to its neighbors, so one hop costs O(1) at any depth, whereas traversing N recursion levels relationally needs N-1 joins and cost grows with every added level.

nodes.label: Evaluation Limits and Future Work
nodes.rationale: Single machine so no network delay, medians of 5-10 runs so no confidence intervals, five hand-picked correctness pairs so no accuracy score, and the whole evaluation runs on data made by the project being tested. Remedies: full-text index on full_name, day-level birthdays, thousands of random test pairs, remote database host - none of which touch the schema or classifier.

nodes.label: Pedigree Graphs and Traversal
nodes.rationale: Pedigrees are DAGs of individuals with parent-child edges; path-based indexes must be rebuilt whenever data changes and direction-optimizing BFS assumes a static distributed graph, both poor fits for a live registry.

nodes.label: Research Gap: Speed vs Legal Transparency
nodes.norm_label: research gap: speed vs legal transparency
nodes.rationale: Static graph indexes must be recomputed on every birth and AI methods are accurate but opaque, while officials need transparent math to justify decisions; no existing system combines graph speed with legal transparency and real-time updates.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Problem Statement and Research Gap

nodes.label: Name-Search Full-Scan Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: CONTAINS cannot use an index; 'hakim' returns in 25.6ms only by luck because LIMIT 20 fills early, while a no-match query must read all 5.13M names at ~2.9s. Worst case is 222x the best case and users reach it with a typo; the fix is a full-text index on full_name.

nodes.label: Four Wives Outside Birth Windows
nodes.rationale: All four out-of-window people are injected wives born 1941-01-01, one year past the founder window - 0.00008% of the dataset, fixable by capping wife birth years at 1940 in the injection utility.

nodes.label: 300ms Debounced Search
nodes.rationale: The search box waits 300ms after the last keystroke, otherwise every letter fires an API request.

nodes.label: nid < sp_nid Ordering Guard
nodes.rationale: Because marriage is stored on both sides, the lexicographic guard makes each MARRIED_TO edge get created exactly once even when one row lists several spouses.

nodes.label: Pipe-Separated spouse_nid Encoding
nodes.rationale: Multiple spouses live in a single CSV column separated by '|' because NIDs are pure digits, so the separator can never collide with a value; each wife stores only her husband's NID, keeping the schema single-column.

nodes.label: Sibling Gap Rule-3 Deviation
nodes.rationale: Child i gets birth year start + i*random(1..4) with an independent roll per child, so two children can land on the same year (read as twins) or more than 4 years apart. Rule 3 holds as a strong tendency (77.8%), not a guarantee; adding each gap to a running year instead of multiplying by the index would make it strict.

nodes.label: 47 System Rules
nodes.rationale: Rules 1-33 govern generation, 34-45 govern relationship reading and input validation, 46-47 came with the multiple-marriage upgrade. Almost every rule mirrors a real Bangladesh fact (legal marriage ages 21/18, 2022 census religion mix, falling fertility) so the synthetic population is defensible.

nodes.label: Two-Pass Batch Import
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 MERGEs every Citizen node, pass 2 creates relationships, so an edge is only created when both endpoints already exist (Rule 44). Batches of 10,000 rows through UNWIND avoid the cost of one transaction per row, and MERGE over CREATE makes re-import idempotent.

nodes.label: Why Synthetic Data
nodes.rationale: Real NID data is legally confidential and a project like this should not try to obtain it, so the population is generated - which imposes the duty of proving both that the rules mirror the real country and that the data obeys the rules.

nodes.label: Hakim Sarker Four-Wife Test Household
nodes.rationale: NID 1926209761584, a founder with four wives and 28 children, used throughout because he exercises the multiple-marriage features harder than an ordinary family.

nodes.label: Rokan Sarker Polygamy Root Test
nodes.rationale: NID 1949207989002; rooting on a child is the only viewpoint that shows half-siblings and step-mothers at once. 6 full siblings, 21 half-siblings, 3 step-mothers and 1 mother, 54 people, no in-law labels - a fault at any layer would show as a wrong count.

nodes.label: categorizeSide Side Categorization
nodes.rationale: Traces ancestors to place a relative on the father's or mother's side; cousins need an extra grandparent hop, otherwise a maternal cousin is wrongly routed to the father's side through the root.

nodes.label: _compute_all_relationships BFS Labeling
nodes.rationale: Builds a direction-annotated adjacency list, BFS from the root for shortest paths, then labels each node via _label_from_path in O(V+E).

nodes.label: /api/family-tree Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Runs a fixed 12-step sequence (root, ancestors, descendants, spouses, siblings, nephews, uncles, cousins, restricted marriage expansion, parent back-fill, edge de-duplication, labeling) so cost stays flat regardless of family size.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Family Tree API - Detailed Logic

nodes.label: _fetch_parents Parent Back-Fill
nodes.rationale: Fills in missing parent edges between people already on the canvas. Without it, all children of a polygynous man would hang off the father alone instead of splitting into one branch per wife.

nodes.label: Parents Map
nodes.rationale: A {nid: {father, mother}} map for everyone on the path; without it the classifier cannot separate full from half siblings, or step-parents from in-laws.

nodes.label: _relationship_detail Detail Line
nodes.rationale: Returns a short explanation shown next to the label ('same father', 'shares husband Karim Ahmed') so the label carries its own proof.

nodes.label: shortestPath Cypher Relationship Query
nodes.rationale: Neo4j shortestPath over HAS_FATHER|HAS_MOTHER|MARRIED_TO capped at 20 hops to keep the query cheap.

nodes.label: Graph Canvas Visual Encoding
nodes.rationale: Every color, ring and line style has a fixed meaning (blue father link, pink mother link, gold curved dash-dot marriage, cyan dashed half-sibling ring, rose co-wife ring, marriage-count badge) so polygynous and step relations are spottable at a glance.

nodes.label: Chandola et al. (2009) Anomaly Detection Survey
nodes.norm_label: chandola et al. (2009) anomaly detection survey

nodes.label: Muller and Axhausen (2011) Hierarchical Population Synthesis
nodes.norm_label: muller and axhausen (2011) hierarchical population synthesis

nodes.label: Bidirectional Search
nodes.rationale: Searching from source and target at once cuts unidirectional O(b^d) to O(b^(d/2)); PBBA applies it to genealogy but assumes a symmetric graph, so it fits deep or disconnected branches poorly.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Path Finding and Relationship Classification

nodes.label: No Authentication or Access Control
nodes.rationale: No authentication, session management or role-based access control, a serious privacy problem for a national database; the biological-parentage schema also cannot represent adoption, foster care or divorce.

nodes.label: Semantic Kinship Constraint Layer
nodes.rationale: A path alone does not name a relationship; a formal semantic layer above the edges can express non-traditional and multi-spouse topologies and separate biological, affinal and step relations. Existing rule engines are strictly Boolean, so one bad historical entry invalidates a valid branch.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Path Finding and Relationship Classification

nodes.label: Synthetic Populations and Temporal Auditing
nodes.rationale: Random generators produce nonsense such as parents younger than their children, so microdata needs deterministic constraints; auditing follows the same logic, where one fixed contextual window such as 270 days catches offending records without scanning the whole graph.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Synthetic Populations and Temporal Auditing

nodes.label: Bounded 10-Level Traversal
nodes.rationale: Ancestor and descendant queries stop at *1..10 so a traversal can never run away into the whole graph.

nodes.label: Count-Based Path Classification Table
nodes.source_location: Table: Relationship classification based on path direction counts

nodes.label: Graph vs Table Deliberate Split
nodes.rationale: The API computes every relative, but the canvas shows only close family to stay readable while the View Table shows everything categorized onto the father's or mother's side.
nodes.source_location: Subsection: Graph vs. Table - A Deliberate Split

nodes.label: 127.0.0.1 vs localhost IPv6 Stall
nodes.rationale: On Windows localhost resolves to ::1 first while the Flask dev server listens on IPv4 only, so every request waits ~2s for the IPv6 attempt to fail. The app felt slow even though the family-tree API answers in ~20ms warm; opening 127.0.0.1:5000 removes the delay entirely.

nodes.label: MIN_BIRTH_GAP_DAYS 270-Day Rule
nodes.rationale: 270 days is roughly a full-term pregnancy: a 0-day gap is twins and allowed, 0<delta<270 is biologically impossible for one mother and gets flagged, and 270 or more is normal.

nodes.label: No-In-Laws Invariant
nodes.rationale: Enforced during data gathering rather than by hiding labels: marriages are expanded only for the root's own spouses and direct parents, so a sibling's spouse or grandparent's second spouse is never fetched at all.

nodes.label: Order-Sensitive Multiple-Marriage Labels
nodes.rationale: SPOUSE+SPOUSE = co-wife, UP+SPOUSE = step-parent, SPOUSE+DOWN = step-child, UP+DOWN with exactly one shared parent = half-sibling.

nodes.label: Rules 46-47 Polygyny Model
nodes.rationale: Only married Muslim men may take up to four wives (2 wives 8%, 3 wives 3%, 4 wives 1%, ~12% overall); all other religions are strictly monogamous. Rates are deliberately generous versus real prevalence so the feature shows up clearly in demos.

nodes.label: Relationship Classification Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Walks the shortest path and reads the sequence of UP/DOWN/SPOUSE moves. Order-sensitive multiple-marriage patterns are checked before count-based rules because move counts alone cannot tell a father's second wife from a wife's mother - both are one parent hop plus one marriage hop.
